summary.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores, with NIM at 9.04% and disbursements up 19.51% YoY to INR49,974 crores.
summary.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q1 FY27 numbers, with PAT of INR3,444.56 crores (up 59.79% YoY, up 14.3% QoQ) and NII up 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores. Growth was supported by fresh equity of about INR39,600 crores, which cut the leverage ratio to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and funded repayment of borrowings. Management reiterated the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% but said it will reassess after Q2, and guided credit cost around 2% and operational NIM around 8.5% in the medium term. Asset quality was broadly stable, with gross Stage 3 at 4.64% against 4.58% in Q4 FY26. Management said the company will now deploy surplus liquidity into growth and return to borrowing, including securitisation, towards the end of the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 CV disbursement INR19,556 crores, the largest product. Management said CV growth tracked the ~20% industry volume growth and new-vehicle share is rising.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 PV disbursement INR11,018 crores. Management cited industry PV sales growth of 25.9%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 MSME disbursement INR6,184 crores. Management targets MSME rising from about 15% to about 20% of the book, with growth expected to exceed the overall book.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 gold disbursement INR5,153 crores; gold is about 2.5% of the book, targeted at about 5% in three years, with about 2,200 branches gold-ready.

segments.name: Personal loans, 2-wheelers, construction and farm equipment
segments.commentary: Personal loans INR2,773 crores, 2-wheelers INR3,548 crores, construction equipment INR792 crores (about INR1,000 crores for five quarters), farm equipment INR947 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% is retained; management will reassess after Q2 FY27 and expects growth of more than 15% in Q2.
Operational NIM expected around 8.5% in the medium term (2-3 years); current NIM of about 9% expected to hold for the next two quarters as surplus liquidity is deployed.
Credit cost guided at around 2% in the near and medium term.
Cost-to-income ratio to remain stable; about 150 branches to be added in FY27 without a material rise in cost.
New vehicle share of disbursement (about 16-17%) expected to rise to about 20-25% over time, with new-vehicle book reaching about 30% plus of the book in the medium term.
Borrowing to resume around the end of Q2 (August to October), with securitisation likely; incremental borrowing cost about 7.77%, bank borrowing about 8%.
capex_capacity: About 150 new branches tentatively planned for FY27, with manpower to rise in line with volume.
About 2,200 branches made ready for gold loan activity; gold book targeted to double in three years.
Surplus liquidity of INR17,000-18,000 crores held as roughly three months of liability repayments; the balance of surplus is expected to be deployed into growth over about 1-1.5 months.
No liability repayments planned from here; borrowing programme to restart, with securitisation and direct assignment transactions not done in Q1.
demand_pricing: Industry: CV sales up 14.1% YoY to 2.65 lakh units; PV up 25.9%; 2-wheelers up 20.3%; 3-wheelers up 29.7%; tractors up 21.6%; construction equipment up 8.8%, per management.
Management said operators have absorbed fuel-cost increases without vehicle idling, and used-vehicle demand has stayed healthy.
Lower borrowing costs are being passed on to new-vehicle customers, and some customers who had left for other lenders are being won back by matching rates.
Management said the MSME slowdown in FY26 was due to US tariffs and policy uncertainty; the book is now expected to grow again from Q2.
Gold demand is driven by customers raising loans against existing jewellery, which management sees as a source of volume for NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the NIM hold at around 9%, given excess liquidity and a slow mix shift toward new vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current NIM should hold for the next two quarters, but will fall to about 8.5% in the medium term as new-vehicle mix rises. Management said the INR500 crore of NII from equity-funded surplus liquidity will gradually subside.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 18% FY27 growth guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management retained 18% for FY27, said it will reassess after Q2, and expects growth above 15% next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for asset quality in gold and MSME?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold asset quality is not a concern, and MSME quality is improving after a cautious year. The Q1 Stage 3 rise was a seasonal impact, from 4.58% to 4.63%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of incremental borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank borrowing would cost about 8%, and incremental capital-market borrowing about 7.77%; the company now borrows as a AA-rated entity, which lowers its cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why will the company borrow again if it holds surplus liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the surplus will be used for growth over about 1-1.5 months, after which fresh borrowing will resume, including securitisation toward the end of the quarter.

risks_watch: Monsoon deficit: rainfall was 24% below normal from June 4 to July 16, and IMD forecasts 90% of normal rainfall for 2026, which could affect rural income and oilseed and pulse output.
West Asia conflict and fuel prices: management said pass-through has held so far, but a further rise in retail fuel prices could hit operator margins.
NIM trajectory: management guides NIM falling from 9.04% to about 8.5% in the medium term, and analysts questioned the pace.
MSME and gold: Stage 3 rose QoQ in gold and MSME; the MSME book must grow to about INR7,000 crores per quarter from Q3 to meet the target.
Borrowing restart: funding will move back toward market borrowings and securitisation after Q2, so the cost of funds and mix will be watched.
Construction equipment disbursement has stayed near INR1,000 crores for five quarters against about INR2,000 crores previously.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and asset quality, but cautious on the guidance path: management held the FY27 target, deferred any upgrade until after Q2, and repeatedly tied the outlook to monsoon and West Asia risk. Questions on the 8.5% medium-term NIM drew the most pushback from analysts.
key_quotes: But we are confident that we'll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.
So our long-term margins of 8.5%, we will be able to manage.
Gold, absolutely not. MSME, we have been cautious in the last 1 year. We are now pretty confident about the MSME quality -- asset quality.
